chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Ismāʿīl al-Jaʿfī, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'A man divorced his wife.' He said, 'He has more right to take her back (revocation of divorce) as long as the blood has not fallen from the third menstruation.'
ai.seo_question: When does the third menstruation finalize a revocable divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of al-Isfahani, this hadith clarifies the precise boundary for revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī) by linking the husband's right of return to the completion of the third menstrual cycle. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that the occurrence of blood from the third period serves as the definitive marker for the divorce becoming final (ba'in), a ruling derived from the interplay of Quranic verses and prophetic practice. This narration is central to the debate between the Ja'fari school and other Sunni schools regarding whether the third period must fully complete or merely begin to finalize the divorce.
